rule.description: A locally defined concept type is fragmented when functions whose signatures mention that type live in at least four distinct modules other than the type's home module: every such function holds a maintenance fragment of the concept, so a conceptual change requires one coordinated edit per module instead of one edit in the owning module.

checks.description: Detect functions located outside the home module of a locally defined concept type that mention the type in their signature, reported for each concept whose fragments span at least four distinct foreign modules.
checks.detected_relation: function in foreign module -> signature mention of a concept type whose home is the row module
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each foreign signature is a place where another module invests in the concept (deriving it, deciding when it applies, budgeting for it, or formatting it), so a conceptual change to the concept must be made in lockstep across all of those modules rather than in the module that owns the concept.

matches.evidence: The configuration module holds the policy fragment: a const predicate that takes the gutter width concept type and decides whether the gutter applies for the current window width.
The terminal module holds the budget fragment: a function that takes the concept type as a parameter and subtracts its padding from the window width to compute the columns left for text.

The escape-sequence module holds the presentation fragment: a generic formatting function that takes the concept type and renders a right-aligned entry followed by the vertical separator bar, alongside the gutter color constant moved there with it.

The editor holds the orchestration fragment: a method on the Editor type that derives the concept value from editor state (row count, configuration, window width) and returns it plus the visibility decision in one accessor.
